title: Ai
lead: A town near Bethel whose name means "the ruin." Abraham camped near it; Israel was defeated there because of Achan, then took it by ambush (Genesis 12:8; Joshua 7–8).

sections.b: Abraham built an altar between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12:8; Genesis 13:3). Israel's first attack on Ai failed because of Achan's sin, and the second, by ambush, succeeded (Joshua 7–8); Joshua made it "a ruin mound forever" (Joshua 8:28). Yet men of Ai returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32), and Isaiah mentions "Aiath" on an invader's road (Isaiah 10:28). Most archaeologists identify it with et-Tell, which was abandoned through the late Bronze Age, making Ai a center of debate over the conquest; a minority, mostly holding the early date, propose Khirbet el-Maqatir instead.
